To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
climate change will lead to a significant increase of the potential distribution of three invasive plant species in New Zealand.
climate change may increase the potential distribution of recently naturalised plant invasions in New Zealand.

climate change may increase habitat suitability for three recently naturalised plants, Archontophoenix cunninghaniana, Psidum guajava and Scheflera actinoplylla, in New Zealand, with potentially suitable areas increasing by 169, 133 and 208 %, respectively, compared to the current habitat.

the potential spread of invasive species under climate change, and the results are useful to assess the potential impacts of climate change on invasive plants in New Zealand, and to identify areas that may require additional control measures.
the development of a methodological approach for modelling the potential spread of invasive species under future climate scenarios and its application to three recently naturalised plants.
the potential spread of invasive plants under climate change, and the implications for management and conservation of biodiversity.
